findings.title: Repeated individuals may cross the evaluation boundary
findings.explanation: Repeated observations were found for person_id. A random row split may mix the same individual across training and test partitions.

evidence.text:
Dataset: cohort.csv
Rows inspected: 960
Columns: signature_0, signature_1, signature_2, signature_3, signature_4, person_id, outcome
Repeated entity rows: {'person_id': 840}
Duplicate rows: 840

alternatives: Row-level evaluation may be appropriate when predicting observations for known individuals
limitations: Entity semantics and intended deployment require human judgment
findings.next_action: Confirm the intended population, then inspect a grouped re-evaluation.

findings.title: New-individual evaluation changes the evidence boundary
findings.explanation: You confirmed that deployment concerns new individuals. The measured baseline shared entities across partitions, while the corrected grouped evaluation kept them separate. Inspect the actual metrics and original/reconstructed classification in both manifests.
alternatives: Group composition and seed variation can also change performance
limitations: The baseline may be original execution or reconstruction, as labeled; the grouped run is an explicitly changed protocol
One corrected split does not establish statistical significance or misconduct
findings.next_action: Review the actual run manifests and evaluate stability across additional group splits before making a broader claim.
